question: How has Nanhai Precision Castings' on-time delivery trended by month?
Which inbound purchase orders are delayed, and by how many days?
What does the AI forecast say for SG-400 demand at Dayton over the next 13 weeks?
How has the weekly fill rate by plant changed over the last 12 weeks?
Which components are projected to stock out in the next 13 weeks, and how much revenue is at risk?
What is our excess and obsolete inventory value by plant?
What approval does an expedite need under the supply policy, and when may we use an alternate source?

content:
Corvane Motion Systems (fictional) makes servo gearmotors (SG-250/400/600), planetary gearboxes (PG-60/90/120), linear actuators (LA-50/90) and motion controllers (MC-10) in three plants: Dayton OH (plant_id DAY), Monterrey MX (MTY) and Wroclaw PL (WRO). The SG-300 servo was sunset at Monterrey in May.
PLANNING HORIZON: 13 weekly buckets starting Monday (week_start). week_index 0 = the current week (the planning as-of date = stockout_exposures.as_of_date). Demand forecast = AI_FORECAST (demand_forecast); component requirements = forecast exploded through the bill of materials.
STOCK-OUTS / EXPOSURES: use stockout_exposures (one row per component x plant that goes below safety stock or negative). exposure_type 'STOCKOUT' = projected balance goes negative; 'BELOW_SAFETY_STOCK' = dips under safety stock only. revenue_at_risk is in USD; peak_units_short is the maximum projected shortage. For week-by-week detail use inventory_projection (projected_balance uses open POs at their revised ETA; balance_if_on_time uses the promised date).
FILL RATE = SUM(units_shipped) / SUM(units_ordered) from gold_fill_rate_weekly (or the metric view mv_supply_performance, measure fill_rate). Always aggregate with SUM ratios, never AVG of fill_rate. gold_fill_rate_weekly.fill_rate is a 0-1 ratio; report it as a percentage (x 100). Target is 97%. The latest week in the data is the last complete week.
SUPPLIER ON-TIME DELIVERY: gold_supplier_performance_monthly.on_time_pct is ALREADY a percentage between 0 and 100 (e.g. 33.3 means 33.3%) — never multiply it by 100; when combining months recompute 100 * SUM(pos_on_time) / SUM(pos_received). It is by month of receipt and only counts RECEIVED POs — an 'on-time delivery trend' question is ALWAYS answered from gold_supplier_performance_monthly, never from open or in-transit POs. For delayed POs that have NOT arrived yet use gold_open_purchase_orders where is_delayed = true (delay_days = revised_eta - promised_date).
EXCESS & OBSOLETE (E&O): gold_inventory_health.eo_value (USD) and eo_category ('Obsolete' = no forward demand and no issue for 90+ days, 'Excess' = more than 26 weeks of cover). Days of supply = gold_inventory_health.days_of_supply.
BOOKED PLANS: sop_plan_decisions holds mitigation plans booked from the Supply Planning Copilot app (plan_cost, revenue_protected, action_summary). It may be empty if nothing was booked yet — say so.
SUPPLY SIGNALS: supplier_signals is ai_extract output over supplier and forwarder emails (event_type, supplier_name, component, po_numbers, added_delay_days, summary).
Format money as USD with thousands separators, percentages with one decimal. Use plant_name (Dayton, Monterrey, Wroclaw) in answers.
ROUTING: numbers, counts, amounts, rates, trends -> query the TABLES (SQL); never answer numbers from a document. Policy, procedure, guideline, contract and 'what does the document say' questions -> search the attached documents and cite the document name + section.

question: How does SG-400 demand at Dayton over the last 8 weeks compare with the same period a year earlier?
sql: SELECT CASE WHEN week_start > (SELECT date_sub(MAX(week_start), 56) FROM manufacturing.supply_planning_copilot.demand_history) THEN 'last 8 weeks' ELSE 'same 8 weeks a year earlier' END AS period, ROUND(AVG(units_ordered), 0) AS avg_weekly_units FROM manufacturing.supply_planning_copilot.demand_history WHERE sku = 'SG-400' AND plant_id = 'DAY' AND (week_start > (SELECT date_sub(MAX(week_start), 56) FROM manufacturing.supply_planning_copilot.demand_history) OR week_start BETWEEN (SELECT date_sub(MAX(week_start), 56 + 364) FROM manufacturing.supply_planning_copilot.demand_history) AND (SELECT date_sub(MAX(week_start), 364) FROM manufacturing.supply_planning_copilot.demand_history)) GROUP BY 1

question: What is our excess and obsolete inventory value by plant?
sql: SELECT plant_name, eo_category, COUNT(*) AS components, SUM(eo_units) AS eo_units, ROUND(SUM(eo_value), 0) AS eo_value FROM manufacturing.supply_planning_copilot.gold_inventory_health WHERE eo_value > 0 GROUP BY plant_name, eo_category ORDER BY eo_value DESC

question: Which inbound purchase orders are delayed, and by how many days?
sql: SELECT po_number, supplier_name, component_id, plant_name, quantity, promised_date, revised_eta, delay_days, delay_reason, vessel FROM manufacturing.supply_planning_copilot.gold_open_purchase_orders WHERE is_delayed ORDER BY delay_days DESC, revised_eta

question: How has Nanhai Precision Castings' on-time delivery trended by month?
sql: SELECT month, pos_received, pos_on_time, on_time_pct, avg_days_late FROM manufacturing.supply_planning_copilot.gold_supplier_performance_monthly WHERE supplier_name = 'Nanhai Precision Castings' ORDER BY month

question: How has the weekly fill rate by plant changed over the last 12 weeks?
sql: SELECT week_start, plant_name, ROUND(100 * SUM(units_shipped) / SUM(units_ordered), 1) AS fill_rate_pct FROM manufacturing.supply_planning_copilot.gold_fill_rate_weekly WHERE week_start > (SELECT date_sub(MAX(week_start), 84) FROM manufacturing.supply_planning_copilot.gold_fill_rate_weekly) GROUP BY week_start, plant_name ORDER BY week_start, plant_name

question: Which components are projected to stock out in the next 13 weeks, and how much revenue is at risk?
sql: SELECT component_id, component_name, plant_name, exposure_type, first_stockout_week, weeks_short, peak_units_short, revenue_at_risk, root_cause, primary_supplier FROM manufacturing.supply_planning_copilot.stockout_exposures ORDER BY revenue_at_risk DESC

question: What does the AI forecast say for SG-400 demand at Dayton over the next 13 weeks?
sql: SELECT week_start, forecast_units, forecast_lower, forecast_upper FROM manufacturing.supply_planning_copilot.demand_forecast WHERE sku = 'SG-400' AND plant_id = 'DAY' ORDER BY week_start
